svg.title: CLAD-Net architecture as implemented in baseline/cladnet
svg.desc: CSPDarknet53 backbone, cross-layer aggregation attention neck (RM + CAM), and an anchor-based decoupled head. Shapes are for a 640x640 input, 2 classes and 3 anchors per level.
svg.text: cross-layer aggregation attention network — as implemented in baseline/cladnet
7.488 M parameters (backbone 4.17 M · neck 2.28 M · heads 1.04 M) — the paper reports 7.5 M. Shapes are C×H×W for a 640×640 input, 2 classes, 3 anchors per level.
stem Conv 1×1 → two parallel branches of Conv 3×3 ×2
anchor-based: 3 anchors per level, decoded as YOLOv5 does
tip — 32 × 32 px box on the tip
the tip box centre is the predicted
yields both AP and hit-rate @ N px
The two modules the paper contributes
reconstructed from Figs. 2–3; every unstated choice is marked PAPER: in common/modules.py
F_y = Conv1×1( Concat[ AAB(F_x) , MSAB(F_x) ] ) — paper Eq. 1
AdaptiveAvgPool → 1, 2, 3, 6 (four scales, each Conv1×1 then upsampled back)
Concat → Conv1×1 → BN → ReLU → Conv3×3 → Sigmoid = f_a
F₁ = f_a ⊗ F_x — handles instruments of very different sizes
pool sizes are not stated in the paper; PSPNet's 1/2/3/6 are used
GCA: GAP → Conv1×1 → BN → ReLU → Conv1×1 = f_g (C × 1 × 1)
LCA: Conv1×1 → BN → ReLU → Conv1×1 = f_l (C × H × W)
F₂ = σ(f_g + f_l) ⊗ F_x — handles low foreground/background contrast
one weight per channel, plus one per channel per pixel
In the neck, CAM also does the channel reduction: concat[ down(N), RM ] 336 ch → F_y 112 ch.
Its trailing 1×1 is the paper's own Conv1, so no block the paper does not describe is inserted.
⊗ element-wise multiply · σ sigmoid · GAP global average pool
F_x = Concat[ ω · F_a , (1 − ω) · F_b ] — paper Eq. 2
ω₁ and ω₂ are each a sigmoid, so ω ∈ [0, 2] and (1 − ω) can go negative — F_b may be subtracted.
Fig. 3 draws a plain sum with nothing squashing it, so that is the default; --rm-combine mean halves it.
Both inputs are aligned to 112 channels by 1×1 convolutions first; the paper never states the channel bookkeeping.
Purpose: rebalance how much detail (lateral) versus semantics (top-down) each level carries.

Zhao et al., "CLAD-Net: cross-layer aggregation attention network for real-time endoscopic instrument detection", Health Inf Sci Syst 11:58 (2023) — no official code; this is a reconstruction from the paper text and Figs. 1–3.
